text:
jordan: Customer reports 401 invalid_api_key only from their service behind our staging Envoy (HTTP/2). curl from their laptop succeeds. Need help triaging.
maria: Did they share a repro request (headers + curl)?
jordan: They sent this curl (redacted key):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_**********************abc123' \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
jordan: curl -v shows Authorization header present and length ~128 chars. But their service logs show upstream Envoy forwarded Authorization truncated to 92 bytes and our auth service returns invalid_api_key.
alex: Can you paste the Envoy access logs or admin stats? curious if there's an http header buffer limit or h2 header compression artifact.
jordan: Pasted from customer (sanitized):
```
[envoy][2026-03-16T14:22:11.123Z] "POST /v1/chat HTTP/2" 401 - "auth: \"Bearer sk_live_**********************a"
```
jordan: Notice the header ends mid-key (cut off at 'a'). curl => full key, service => truncated.
envoy-bot: Notice: http2 protocol used between service and Envoy (upstream). HPACK header compression negotiated.
maria: Two quick asks: 1) are there any per-route header size limits in their Envoy config? 2) do they have a proxy/WAF that strips long header values?
jordan: They checked and have a per-route buffer tuned down for memory. Config snippet they shared: `max_request_headers_kb: 8` and `http2_protocol_options: { header_table_size: 4096 }` (customer sanitized).
alex: That combination can lead to HPACK dynamic table eviction and, in some older Envoy builds, truncated header frames when buffers are low. TL;DR: header value can be cut if upstream buffer limit is hit during HPACK decoding.
maria: Workarounds: 1) increase max header buffer (eg 32kb) or remove aggressive per-route header limit; 2) disable http2 header compression for that route; 3) as a short-term workaround, send the API key in `x-api-key` (Envoy currently forwards that intact for them).
jordan: Customer applied increase to `max_request_headers_kb` to 32 and restarted Envoy. They reported immediate success: calls now auth succeed.
jordan: Customer confirmed :white_check_mark: "rolling back the small header buffer fixed it, thanks"
alex: Filing a follow-up bug note: older Envoy versions + low header buffers + large API keys can cause HPACK truncation leading to 401s. Recommend we add a KB entry and a diagnostic checklist. Ticket: INT-2026-1147.
maria: Great. Add repro steps and minimal config snippet to the ticket so support can triage faster next time.
jordan: Done, uploaded logs to INT-2026-1147 and marked resolved with customer.
